title: Encounter Propagator for Multiple Targets: A Dirichlet-to-Neumann Spectral Formalism
abstract: We develop an encounter-based formulation of restricted diffusion in a bounded domain with multiple targets, resolving separately the boundary local time accumulated on each target. Unlike the single-target problem, the target projection operators do not generally commute with the governing Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) operator, so that its eigenbasis does not diagonalize the local-time dependence. We overcome this difficulty by decomposing the DtN operator into target-restricted blocks. Multi-dimensional Laplace inversion then yields a convergent switching expansion, whose successive terms describe alternating diffusive transfers between the targets. We also derive an equivalent operator-valued renewal equation. For two targets, diagonalizing the target-restricted blocks provides an explicit spectral representation in terms of two DtN block spectra and an inter-target coupling matrix. When the coupling preserves spectral modes, the switching series can be resummed exactly in terms of modified Bessel functions. In general, as the off-diagonal DtN block is smoothing for separated targets, one can resort to low-rank finite-dimensional approximations. We examine an effective two-mode reduction for small, well-separated targets and identify a regime in which repeated inter-target transfers are progressively suppressed. Probabilistic interpretations and implications for diffusion-controlled reactions are discussed.
summary: This paper develops a spectral formalism to calculate the encounter propagator for diffusion processes encountering multiple distinct targets on a boundary. By decomposing the governing Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator into target-specific blocks, the authors overcome mathematical difficulties associated with non-commuting operators. The resulting framework yields an exact spectral representation for the two-target case, providing deep insights into diffusion-controlled reaction rates.
main_problem: Developing a rigorous, spectral formulation for the encounter propagator in restricted diffusion within a bounded domain containing multiple reactive targets.
main_result: The authors derive a convergent switching expansion for the propagator, providing explicit spectral representations for the two-target case, which can be resummed exactly using modified Bessel functions under certain conditions.
method: The methodology involves decomposing the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) operator into target-restricted blocks and performing multi-dimensional Laplace inversion to handle the joint local-time dependence.
model_or_system: The model is restricted diffusion in a bounded domain $\Omega$ with multiple targets $\Gamma_i$ on the boundary. The physics is governed by the diffusion equation with complex boundary conditions related to local time accumulation.
key_observables: The encounter propagator $P(x, \ell_1, \dots, \ell_N, t|x_0)$ and its Laplace transform $eP(x, \ell_1, \dots, \ell_N, p|x_0)$.
important_parameters: The number of targets ($N$), the separation distance between targets, and the Laplace variable $p$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on decomposing the DtN operator into blocks and assumes conditions (like separation) that allow for spectral diagonalization or low-rank approximations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the two-target encounter problem, partitioning the boundary into reflecting and reactive target regions ($\Gamma_1, \Gamma_2$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the single-target case to the multi-target generalization, focusing on decomposing the DtN operator, deriving the switching expansion via multi-dimensional Laplace inversion, and finally presenting spectral representations and asymptotic analyses for the two-target case.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical treatment of non-commuting operators (DtN vs. projection operators) and the resulting spectral methods are highly relevant for modeling open quantum systems where dissipation or coupling to multiple baths/channels occurs.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic representation of the two-target encounter problem in a planar bounded domain Ω, whose boundary ∂Ω is partitioned into the reﬂecting part Γ0 and two target regions Γ1 and Γ2. During a given time t, the particle diﬀuses from a point x0 to a point x, and accumulates boundary local times ℓ1,t and ℓ2,t on the target regions Γ1 and Γ2. Four representative cases are shown: (a) ℓ1,t = 0, ℓ2,t = 0; (b) ℓ1,t > 0, ℓ2,t = 0; (c) ℓ1,t = 0, ℓ2,t > 0; and (d) ℓ1,t > 0, ℓ2,t > 0. Blue curve shows a simulated random trajectory in each case.
